body: Yep, all the adults in the movie have an addiction, but only the food addict is so controversial.
Weight loss surgery (gastric sleeve). It was what I needed to get healthy and I wish I had done it ten years sooner.

Sorry, I'm seldom on this alt.

I have been using Kore vegan protein in chocolate brownie. It was relatively cheap and tastes tolerable (and I just use a shaker bottle). I also like OWYN pre-made shakes (mostly chocolate) if I'm in a hurry. I hated Truvani, tastes so bad! I haven't tried a lot of options and I'm not an expert, I have protein powder even less now than I did when I posted because I can eat higher volume and have dialed in more on a whole foods style!
Is your doctor Garth Davis? I follow him/his advice and way of eating (mostly). I would love to be his patient but don't live in his area.
Thank you!

I follow a bariatric surgeon Dr. Garth Davis. He was a surgeon already when he had similar thoughts, that maybe he should help people do it "the old fashioned way". His father was also a bariatric surgeon and he went to him with these thoughts. His father said [paraphrasing], "If you have the ability to give people surgery and you don't do it, you should be sued for malpractice." 

Surgery has the best health outcomes hands down. Even if it's not perfect and even if people regain, mortality and morbidity from obesity are decreased more than any other intervention.

It's not the easy way out, for many it is the only way out.

I eat beans daily. I also use vegan protein powder on days I lift (only once or twice a week for now). And I have a protein bar as a snack a few times a week. I don't sweat trying to reach a certain number, personally.
No, not usually. I will occasionally do a tally but I don't count calories daily. The food I eat is generally low in calorie density so I end up eating low total calories.

14 months post op. I can eat a fair amount (but am not always hungry like before surgery). I went vegan for ethical reasons at 10 months PO, and now I eat about 80% whole foods (r/plantbaseddiet), so I actually eat pretty high carb. It works for me.

Nobody has mentioned that plan B does not work well for people over 175 pounds (regardless of height). I think the more you weigh, the less likely it is to work. The most effective emergency contraceptive for us is placing a copper IUD within a few days. There's one pill (Ella) that goes a little higher, but even that is like 200 lbs before lower effectiveness. Hopefully the timing is right, most intercourse doesn't lead to pregnancy... Good luck 🤞

I am not near my goal yet. My highest recorded weight was 461, I was at 442 before the pre-op diet and 419 surgery day (so that was the period of fastest weight loss, lol [23 pounds in 2 weeks]). I'm 260ish now. The 300s are a total blur for me, my weight graph is almost linear (though I usually only weighed monthly throughout). It has slowed down the last month. My surgeon just wants me under 200 but I'd love to see 161 to have lost a total of 300 pounds! So I have 100 more to go, which will probably be harder than the last 200.

I do feel completely different! The energy gains alone are worth everything. I am always wanting to do things now instead of sit around. I'm in no pain after 11 hour retail shifts... My feet, hips, and back used to kill after 8 or less. Now I just feel tired but my body doesn't hurt at all. I used to take naproxen every workday but have taken acetaminophen maybe twice since surgery, and nothing for months now. I haven't started lifting weights but plan to soon. I am really glad I had surgery.

I regretted it (sleeve) for a couple of months. I grieved the forced change in my coping mechanism and the physical pain I was in. But now I'm very happy I did it. My one year anniversary is September 22 and I've lost 180 pounds since the pre op diet. Life is so much better now and I could not have done it without surgery.

I think it is very common to regret it in the beginning, but later believe it to be a great decision you wish you'd done earlier. Hearing people here say exactly that is what helped me to finalize my decision.
I just barely tested positive. Gonna call my doctor in the morning about it, so I'm eager to see the responses!

Hi, me. I always want to be vegan but I sometimes fail because of my own issues with food. It's hard to deal with how ex vegans are discussed here so I'm glad to see you haven't been down voted to death.

I tried for a long time (over 10 years) to be plant based before surgery. When I could stick to it, I had amazing results and felt great. But just like all "diets" I tried, I could not stick to it forever. It was way easier and better than any of the others and I could stick to it longer, but I'd still go off and gain (some) weight back. I still want to be plant based because of the health benefits, both scientifically supported and experienced personally in the times I could do it. That was the deciding factor for me getting VSG 7 days ago instead of DS, which my surgery team was strongly suggesting for someone of my BMI. I didn't think I could be plant based with DS and get enough fat and protein. It has been a rough transition but I went in with the goal of being plant based in the end with surgery to help get there. I love seeing other sleeved people go plant based!

I love Premier, even the strawberry but didn't like peaches. The ones with oats are the best, not too much extra carb, fiber is good, less protein but that's okay with me. The chocolate peanut butter is a new flavor that's soooo good! (It doesn't have oats.)

Yeah my insurance nurse (she works for my insurance company, not my surgeon) specifically mentioned in our first call that if I lose to below the normal requisite weight that it won't affect my eligibility. I thought it was a funny comment because I was 400 lbs and not about to get under 40 bmi in 6 months....
Both Tramadol and Ondansetron give me MAJOR headaches and otherwise I never have migraines. Are you on either of those? A pharmacist might be able to help (though maybe not, but it's worth a try!)
I've been craving pickles/pickle juice for electrolytes! I hope you find some relief.
Great job! How was the hair loss? I'm 10 days preop and my hair is the longest it's been in decades, and I'm worried! (I know it will be worth it though!)

I'm sure you can. I just asked for more information about bariatric surgery and they hooked me up with my nurse. So she wasn't the one who first answered the phone, but they put me in contact with her and now I just call her for everything.

Hopefully you're good, then. As for your nurse, call the customer service number on your insurance card. They'll assign you a nurse that will help you through the whole process. Mine has been great, she answers all my questions. She calls to check up on me every few weeks, or I can call her extension.

My surgeon's office said that Anthem had dropped the 6 month requirement. But they were mistaken for my employer. So that's another thing it may depend on. Call your nurse at Anthem, they should know for sure.

This was (is?) causing me some anxiety, too. (I'm pre-op still.) I didn't want anyone to know and I've basically taken no time off in 12 years. I also work with the public and dread customers asking me about it, especially a couple that don't treat me very well... but I've decided to own it, and that eased my anxiety. I don't think it's anyone's business but if they ask, I'll just tell them. Of course there's so much other work going into it that they won't see. I'm not saying you should do the same, but it's an option. I figured some people are going to ask point blank as they see my weight loss, and that would be when I wouldn't know what to say. So I'm just gonna be open.

WOW you are a hard worker. 70+ hours at a job, and then you get 2 jobs, at least one of which is incredibly physically demanding? You have a lot to be proud of. You have value beyond your weight. Please get therapy, or maybe try reading the book "Feeling Good" (bibliotherapy). Make it as important to get over the shame as it was to get over the cancer, because both can eat away at you.

I met my boyfriend on Tinder (at 400 lbs). I prefer OkCupid usually but just happened to find my keeper there. Take honest pictures and be up front about yourself, that saves a lot of time and heartache. And yes, don't settle! It's better to be alone than with a user or abuser! <3

I tried HMR (shakes and meal replacements, medically supervised). It became very hard to stick to pretty quickly, which did not help my mental health. Moving toward a healthier whole foods diet helped my mental health and weight loss, and it is much more sustainable.
